dataset_family: Duke 'OCTA in MCI and AD' study (NCT03233646; Duke IRB Pro00082598), Duke Neurological Disorders Clinics + Duke Alzheimer's Disease Prevention Registry, USA; 67 AD / 74 MCI / 137 controls. Same study family as P-163 (NCT03233646) and P-1317 (Pro00082598), neither a current VF-18 supporter
method_family: Enhanced-depth spectral-domain OCT (Zeiss Cirrus HD-5000) choroidal morphometry: manual SFCT; TCA, LA and CVI by Niblack binarization in ImageJ; multivariable GEE group comparison (age, sex, logMAR VA)
what_it_shows: In clinically diagnosed MCI (NIA-AA, memory specialist), EDI-OCT choroidal parameters differed from controls after adjustment for age, sex and VA: TCA and LA were greater and CVI lower in MCI. SFCT did not differ between MCI and controls, no choroidal parameter correlated with MMSE, there was no classification, and the authors state that overlap was large and discriminative value unclear.
why: PDF identity confirmed: title, the 11 authors (Robbins ... Fekrat), Am J Ophthalmol 2021;223:359-367 and DOI 10.1016/j.ajo.2020.09.049 match the block's Author list, Venue and DOI. The block's own header title is a paraphrase, not the printed title. STATED FORM: partly, and the weakest of the four candidates. It is an ocular-structure channel, but the choroid is the vascular layer beneath the retina, not retinal structure. It fits 'ocular channels (retinal structure, ...)' only if the parenthetical is read as examples; the authors themselves loosely call it 'retinal imaging' (p.7). If 'retinal structure' is read strictly, the verdict is 'no'. On its own data, MCI-versus-control differences in TCA, LA and CVI are significant after adjustment (Table 2, p.5). Against a 'biomarker direction for early cognitive decline': (1) the authors state that differences were small, measurement overlapped, and 'it was unclear whether these parameters might serve as discriminative, objective biomarkers' (pp.4, 6). (2) No choroidal parameter correlated with MMSE. (3) The pattern is not monotonic along the continuum: TCA and LA are larger in MCI than in AD, and CVI is lower only in MCI, not in AD. (4) SFCT, the most-studied parameter, shows no MCI-control difference (the basis of IA-27). (5) Education differed between MCI and controls (15.58 vs 17.12 years, p<.001) and was not a covariate, and axial length was not measured, which the authors concede. There is no discrimination analysis, and scalability is not addressed; EDI-OCT was done in a specialist clinic. Decoding note: the Elsevier extract drops the minus sign in the results text ('CVI was lower ... (ß = 0.58; p = .002)'). The abstract renders it 'ß [ L0.58', and Table 2 means (MCI 63.2% vs control 63.8%) confirm the negative direction. NARROWED FORM: partly. It is a preliminary, single-centre association of an ocular measure with MCI, which matches the head clause. But the narrowed retinal clause is about imaging that 'discriminated MCI', and this study reports no discrimination and measures the choroid rather than the retina. Admitting it would require the wording to add 'choroidal OCT parameters differed at group level in one US clinic cohort'. INDEPENDENCE: no overlap with P-5 (China), P-952 (Shenzhen), P-966 (KIOM/GARD Korea) or P-105 (review), and none with the other VF-18 candidates (P-169 Hanyang, P-998 Tehran, P-282 Mayo). Verified from the PDFs: P-163 (Wisely et al., CNN on multimodal retinal imaging) cites the same NCT03233646, and P-1317 (Joseph et al., UWF retinal/choroidal vasculature) cites the same Duke IRB Pro00082598. Both share authors (Robbins, Grewal, Fekrat; Liu on P-163). They are one Duke dataset family, which counts once if any of them is admitted. Not a preprint. BLOCK/REGISTRY DEFECT: the block's 'What is the sample size?' reads '150 (target) - STUDY PROTOCOL; target enrollment 50 DS/50 MCI/50 HC', which contradicts the block's own first section and the PDF (67 AD/74 MCI/137 controls = 278 participants). Registry Sample_N_Approx '150 (target)' inherits the error.

quotes.quote: Participants included 67 patients (112 eyes) with AD, 74 patients (143 eyes) with MCI, and 137 (248 eyes) control subjects.
THIS CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY (OCTA IN MILD COGNITIVE Impairment and Alzheimer’s Disease; NCT03233646) was approved by the Duke Health Institutional Review Board (Pro00082598)

TCA was significantly higher in subjects with AD versus control subjects (ß = 2.73; p = .001) and in subjects with MCI versus control subjects (ß = 4.38; p < .001) in multivariable analysis. [extract glyph '¼' decoded as '=' and ligature 'fi' restored]

LA was significantly higher in subjects with AD versus control subjects (ß = 1.68; p = .001) and in subjects with MCI versus control subjects (ß = 2.69; p < .001) in multivariable analysis. [same decoding]

CVI did not differ between subjects with AD and control subjects; however, CVI was lower in subjects with MCI versus control subjects in multivariable analysis (ß = 0.58; p = .002). [minus sign dropped by the extract; abstract p.1 prints 'ß [ L0.58', i.e. -0.58]
SFCT was not significantly different between subjects with MCI and control subjects
No statistically significant correlation was found between any choroidal structural parameter (SFCT, TCA, LA, CVI) and MMSE score (all p > .05).

Differences in choroidal parameters between diagnostic groups were small, and measurement overlap did exist between eyes of different diagnostic groups. Thus, although choroidal structure might have significantly varied between subjects with AD and subjects with MCI compared with control subjects, [p.6 continues:] it was unclear whether these parameters might serve as discriminative, objective biomarkers of disease presence.
